key_insight: MUMINS forecasts medical image next-state changes by jointly synthesizing the follow-up scan and an uncertainty map in one diffusion pass, while using the baseline scan as a soft anchor.
clinical_relevance: This could support more informative longitudinal imaging workflows by showing both likely anatomical progression and where the model is least certain.
method: Diffuses the baseline scan and follow-up residual together, then sums them to reconstruct the follow-up image.
Conditions generation on time interval and metadata, with the baseline re-injected at each denoising step to preserve anatomy.
Uses a negative-log-likelihood head to predict a spatial uncertainty map alongside the image output.
evidence_signal: In evaluations on lung CT (PNG) and brain MRI (OASIS-3), dataset-specific retraining of MUMINS matched or outperformed dedicated state-of-the-art methods.
watch_item: Performance depends on dataset-specific retraining, so generalization to new organs, scanners, or institutions may require careful re-validation.
paper_title: MUMINS: Metadata-conditioned Uncertainty-aware Medical Image Next-state Synthesis
